Name: Palomar Knot
Description: A dependable connection for hooks, rings and lures. The doubled line spreads the load and is especially suitable for braid.
Tips: Keep both strands parallel and wet the knot before final tightening.
Etapes: Double about 25 cm of line and pass the loop through the eye.|Tie a very loose overhand knot with the doubled line.|Draw out the large loop without twisting the two strands.|Pass the entire hook or lure through the large loop.|Bring the loop over the eye and behind the hook.|Wet the knot and pull the standing line and tag together.|Check that both strands remain parallel, then trim the tag.

Name: Uni Knot (Grinner)
Description: A versatile knot for attaching line to a hook, swivel or lure. It works with most monofilament and braided lines.
Tips: Make a large loop and form five to seven even turns.
Etapes: Pass the tag through the eye and leave about 20 cm.|Fold the tag back to form a large loop parallel to the standing line.|Make 5 to 7 turns inside the loop around both strands.|Wet the knot and pull the tag so the coils sit side by side.|Slide the knot to the eye, tighten, and trim the tag.

Name: Improved Clinch Knot
Description: A compact connection for hooks, clips and small lures. The final pass locks the wraps around the standing line.
Tips: Make five to seven turns without overlapping the wraps.
Etapes: Pass 15 to 20 cm of line through the eye.|Wrap the tag 5 to 7 times around the standing line.|Feed the tag through the small loop directly above the eye.|Then pass the tag through the large loop that has just formed.|Wet the knot, pull the standing line gradually, and trim the tag.

Name: Rapala Knot
Description: A non-slip loop that lets hard lures and light jigs move freely. The loop diameter remains fixed after tightening.
Tips: Set the loop size before tightening the wraps.
Etapes: Tie a loose overhand knot, pass the tag through the lure eye, then back through the knot.|Make 3 even turns around the standing line.|Pass the tag back through the overhand knot and then through the new large loop.|Wet and tighten while keeping the small loop in front of the lure open.

Name: Blood Knot
Description: A symmetrical join for two monofilaments of similar diameter. The opposing wraps lock together at the centre.
Required Material: Two similar mono or fluoro lines
Tips: Use the same number of turns on both sides and tighten wet.
Etapes: Overlap the two lines by 15 cm and hold their crossing point.|Wrap the first tag 5 to 7 times around the opposite line.|Bring that tag back to the center and through the gap between the lines.|Wrap the other tag 5 to 7 times in the opposite direction.|Feed the second tag through the same center gap in the opposite direction.|Wet the knot and slowly pull both standing lines to bring the coils together.|Trim both tags a few millimeters from the knot.|Check that both sets of coils are symmetrical and tightly packed.

Name: Albright Knot
Description: A compact join between a thin main line and a thicker leader. It suits different materials and diameters.
Tips: The thin tag must enter and leave on the same side of the heavy-line loop.
Etapes: Make a loop in the thicker line and pass the thinner line through it.|Wrap the thin line 8 to 12 times around both legs of the loop.|Work back toward the entry point, keeping every wrap snug.|Feed the thin tag back through the loop on the same side where it entered.|Wet and pull the standing lines gradually to align the wraps.|Tighten firmly and trim both tags close to the knot.

Name: FG Knot
Description: A very slim friction connection where tensioned braid alternates around the leader. It passes cleanly through guides with long leaders.
Tips: Keep strong tension through every crossing and finish with half hitches.
Etapes: Hold the fluorocarbon leader under firm tension and cross the braid over it.|Alternate the braid left and right around the leader to make 16 to 22 tight crossings.|Tension the braid after every crossing so the wraps bite into the leader.|Lock the weave with a half hitch around both the braid and leader.|Tie a second half hitch in the opposite direction and pull both lines very firmly.|The leader should show a light impression under the wraps without being crushed.|Trim the leader flush without damaging the braid.|Finish with 3 to 5 alternating half hitches around the braid only, then trim.

Name: Dropper Loop
Description: A perpendicular loop in the main line for presenting a side hook without a swivel. Suitable for multi-bait rigs.
Tips: Keep the turns together and pass the loop through their centre.
Etapes: Form a large loop at the chosen point on the leader.|Rotate the crossing point 5 to 8 times without twisting the future dropper.|Push the original loop through the center opening made by the turns.|Wet and pull both standing ends and the dropper at the same time.

Name: Three-way Swivel Rig
Description: A three-direction rig separating main line, sinker and hook leader. It reduces tangles while casting and in current.
Tips: Match leader length to the current and check every connection.
Etapes: Tie the main line to the upper eye of the three-way swivel.|Use a Uni or Clinch suited to the line diameter.|Tighten the first knot and check that the eye moves freely.|Tie the hook leader to the side eye.|Tighten the second knot and trim its tag.|Attach the sinker to a shorter dropper tied to the lower eye.|Attach the hook or lure to the end of the side leader.|Check that all three branches swivel freely and cannot cross.

Name: Yucatan Knot
Description: A quick join between a doubled main line and a heavier leader. Useful when a strong connection must be tied at sea.
Required Material: Doubled line and mono or fluoro leader
Tips: Both leader ends must exit together before tightening.
Etapes: Double 20 cm of main line and place the leader alongside the doubled line.|Wrap the doubled line around the leader 4 to 6 times for mono or 8 to 10 times for braid.|Pass the leader tag through the end of the doubled loop.|Wet and pull the leader and both legs of the doubled main line.|Draw the wraps together into a compact, even barrel.|Trim only after a firm pull test.

Name: Snell Knot
Description: An in-line attachment along the hook shank, especially useful with circle hooks. Pull is applied in line with the hook.
Required Material: Mono or fluorocarbon and eyed hook
Tips: For circle hooks, route the standing line toward the hook point.
Etapes: Pass the line through the eye from the hook-point side and leave a large loop.|Lay the standing line straight along the hook shank.|Hold the loop and begin wrapping it around the shank and standing line.|Make 6 to 8 close turns toward the bend.|Keep each turn flat and prevent overlapping.|Wet and pull the standing line to close the loop and tighten the wraps.|Check that the line exits in line with the hook shank.

Name: Perfection Loop
Description: A fixed in-line loop for leaders, clips and loop-to-loop connections.
Tips: Hold the small loop between your fingers during the final pass.
Etapes: Make a first loop by taking the tag behind the standing line.|Make a second loop in front of the first without tightening.|Place the tag between the two loops.|Pull the first loop through the second while holding the tag.|Wet, tighten by pulling the loop and standing line, then trim.

Name: Bimini Twist
Description: Creates a long doubled-line loop while retaining excellent strength. A classic foundation for offshore trolling leaders.
Required Material: Mono or braid and a support point
Tips: Maintain constant tension and spread the twists before the finishing hitches.
Etapes: Double the line to make a large loop, then add 20 to 30 twists.|Hold the loop spread and under tension so the twists travel downward.|Hold the tag at a right angle and let it spiral tightly back over the twists.|Lock first with a half hitch around one leg of the loop.|Then tie a half hitch around both legs.|Repeat the lock and finish with 3 to 5 finishing turns.|Tighten each hitch separately and trim without nicking the doubled line.

Name: San Diego Jam Knot
Description: A powerful terminal knot popularised by tuna anglers. Multiple wraps tighten around two parallel strands.
Tips: Use fewer turns with heavy line and lubricate before tightening.
Etapes: Pass the tag through the eye and fold it parallel to the standing line.|Wrap the tag 5 to 7 times around both lines toward the eye.|Pass the tag through the small loop next to the eye.|Then pass it through the large loop above the wraps.|Wet and tighten by pulling the standing line and tag alternately.|Slide the knot against the eye and trim the tag.

Name: Offshore Swivel Knot
Description: Connects a doubled line to a heavy swivel. The swivel passes through the loop several times before the knot is seated.
Tips: Make three to six passes for the line diameter and tighten evenly.
Etapes: Double the line and pass the resulting loop through the swivel eye.|Open the loop wide and pass the swivel through it.|Rotate the swivel 4 to 6 times through the loop while keeping both strands parallel.|Wet and pull the doubled line so the twists seat against the eye.|Tighten firmly and check that both legs share the load evenly.
